name: Powkiddy V20

pad.note: oakMOSS's adc-joypad driver (DT adc_gamepad), found by name (POWKIDDY_PAD_NAME, set in V20.cfg). V20.cfg's own comment says this platform is 'UNTESTED, carried from the V90S'; a 2026-11-01 simulated run (not hardware) failed to resolve this node at all, which is consistent with no lab unit yet rather than a wrong name.

lradc.note: shared PowkiddyCommon.cfg path; hardware-verified on the V90S (same board family) but not on a V20 unit

power.note: shared PowkiddyCommon.cfg pattern match; hardware-verified on the V90S, not on a V20 unit. A 2026-11-01 simulated run resolved power to a node it printed as 'Power Button' instead - likely an artifact of that simulation rather than real hardware, but worth rechecking on a unit.

L3.note: V20.cfg's own override, over PowkiddyCommon's lack of L3/R3; the research survey (2026-10-23) places L3/R3 on PD21/PD20 on Knulli's 5.15 kernel only, not in the stock DT - oakMOSS's own kernel/DT wiring for this board is unconfirmed

R3.note: see L3; the V20 research survey also flags PD20 as the V90S's rumble PWM pin, repurposed as R3 here - unverified on oakMOSS's own tree

RIGHT_STICK.note: the research survey flags that Knulli's V20 tree swaps the right stick's two axes vs this ordering - confirm on a unit

absent.FN_SWITCH: no switch; device_get_switch_position is the oakMOSS no-op stub (PowkiddyCommon.sh does not override it)
absent.LID: vertical slab, not a clamshell; no hall node for this board in the stock DT survey (n/a, unlike the V90S's disabled MH248 node)

notes: No lab unit of the V20 exists yet as of the 2026-10-23 research and the 2026-11-01 simulated runs; every control here is cfg-only, carried from the V90S by board-family similarity (same stock firmware, same adc-joypad DT pattern) rather than measured. Treat this whole manifest as the weakest-evidenced of the six and re-verify wholesale on first hardware contact.

A 2026-11-01 simulated test run ('oak-rename'/'oak-rebase') FAILED to resolve the V20's pad node and reported POWER on an unexpected node name; both read as simulation artifacts (no real device attached) rather than hardware facts, but are worth re-checking once a unit exists.
A hardware run should settle: L3/R3 presence and codes (PD21/PD20 per the kernel survey, vs Knulli's 5.15-only wiring), the right stick's axis order, and whether POWER truly resolves to axp2202-pek.
